messages:
marco (eng-infra): Quick heads up — scheduling a maintenance window for APAC-west2 on Tue 03:00-04:30 local. Scope: rack-level NVMe/fw microflip + kernel soft-reboot (no full power cycles). We'll do staggered, cohort-based drains to avoid hotspots. Expected steady capacity hit ~10-15% while cohorts rotate. Ping if that conflicts with tenant cutovers. :calendar:

anya (infra-scheduler): Are we excluding priority-tenants and Dedicated pools? Also, what's the exact cohort cadence?

marco (eng-infra): Yes — priority-tenants pinned (exclude via pool label), Dedicated pools are not part of this window. Cadence: 6 cohorts, 10m drain/cordon + 5m warmup per cohort. Sequence: saturn-3 (canary) -> saturn-4 -> saturn-1 ... final backfill. Total per-rack window ~14-16m.

sam (platform): Routing question — do we plan cross-region failover during canaries? Could we route short-burst traffic to us-west1 while saturn-3 is drained? Concerned about latency-sensitive workloads.

marco (eng-infra): Good call. Routing policy 'maintenance-redirect' will send best-effort non-priority traffic to us-west1 for the 30m canary phase, then roll back. Latency SLAs remain for priority tenants (they stay local). We'll update load-balancer weights and pre-warm KV cache for hot prefixes.

cost-ops-liz: Heads up on cost impact: estimate ~$1.2k extra cross-region egress + spot buffer for backfill if we burst to eu/us. That's worst-case if we route 60% of APAC traffic out for 30m. If we can cap at 20% we drop to ~$350. Recommend we enable egress-throttle at 40%.

sam (platform): Throttle sounds reasonable. Which flags are we toggling?

marco (eng-infra): We'll flip the route weights and set egress-throttle = 0.4 on the maintenance-redirect policy. I'll post the exact command in a sec.

marco (eng-infra): Command snippet for the drain step (canary example):
```
# cordon + drain a node gracefully (saturn-3 canary)
kubectl cordon node/saturn-3-rack-01
kubectl drain node/saturn-3-rack-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=10m
```
Note: we use --timeout 10m so the orchestrator can evict without blocking the cohort.

oncall-karen: I'll be on rotation that night. I'll watch autoscaler and alerts. If we see >20% queued requests for any p99 path, I escalate to marco and trigger rollback.

deploy-bot: Scheduled: rolling-maintenance-apac-west2 saturn-cohort 2026-06-08T03:00Z -> 2026-06-08T04:30Z (owner: marco)

anya (infra-scheduler): Runbook link and checklist?

marco (eng-infra): Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/maintenance/apac-west2-rack-fw-2026 Steps include preflight checks (disk-health, nvme firmware diff, kernel compat), canary verification (latency, kv-hit rate), and fallback plan (pause rollout + instant route rollback). I'll attach the preflight gate below:

Preflight quick checklist:
- verify disk SMART PASS on cohort nodes
- ensure KV cache seed hit-rate >= 85%
- verify scheduler backfill capacity >= 12% spare
- alerting: p95 latency + queue depth dashboards visible
- confirm priority pools pinned (label: redwood.priority=high)

sam (platform): One more ask — can we avoid warming all KV prefixes to limit cross-region loads? Maybe only seed top 5 prefixes.

marco (eng-infra): Yes — we'll restrict seed to top-5 hot prefixes for the canary phase. Full warm on later cohorts once we confirm no regressions.

cost-ops-liz: I'll be on slack during the window. If costs deviate >25% from estimate, we'll pause further cohorts.

marco (eng-infra): Sounds good. Action items:
- anya: post calendar notice + update maintenance-redirect policy TTL (by EOD)
- sam: set egress-throttle to 0.4 and prepare LB weight script (1h before)
- oncall-karen: monitor and own escalation
- cost-ops-liz: cost watch during window

marco (eng-infra): If no objections I'll proceed with the scheduled window and run the canary at 03:00. Will ping #general 30m before start. :white_check_mark:
